title: Headroom pulse adapter and provision quiesce controller
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a pulse-based headroom estimator and a provision quiesce controller to reduce autoscaler oscillations and improve tail latency during bursty traffic. Backwards compatible runtime config flags; no customer API changes.
description: Motivation: We observed recurring autoscaler thrash when fleets receive short, high-amplitude bursts. Traditional exponential smoothing on utilization lags or overshoots because the signal is highly non-stationary for these workloads. This PR introduces two coordinated controls: 1) a pulse-based headroom adapter that treats short bursts as discrete pulses and computes transient headroom using a pulse energy model, and 2) a provision quiesce controller that enforces a configurable quiesce window before decommitting capacity to prevent premature scale-downs. Design: The pulse adapter runs alongside the existing estimator and provides an additive headroom suggestion when it detects pulses based on short-term burst detection (peak/median ratio, derivative energy). It exposes tunables: pulse_window_ms, energy_threshold, max_pulse_headroom_pct, and decay_tau_ms. The quiesce controller attaches to decommit flows and delays scale-down actions for a jitter-tolerant window that decays per-tenant based on recent pulse frequency. Config: New runtime feature flags (autoscaler.pulse_adapter.enabled, autoscaler.quiesce.window_ms, autoscaler.quiesce.adaptive) are default-off for safety. Migration & rollout: Feature gated behind canary config; default disabled on all production fleets. We will enable in Canary region for 72 hours with observability hooks enabled and automated rollback on tail-latency regression. Metrics & telemetry: Adds metrics.autoscaler.pulse_detected_total, metrics.autoscaler.pulse_energy_gauge, metrics.autoscaler.quiesce_delay_seconds, and a headroom.source tag for attribution. Tests: unit tests for pulse detection, integration test simulating bursty request traces, and a small e2e canary harness that exercises scale-up/scale-down invariants. Backwards compatibility: If disabled, behavior is identical to main autoscaler. Performance: lightweight signal processing on the sample stream; tested <1% CPU overhead in microbenchmarks. See linked tests and dashboards. This PR includes docs for config knobs and a recommended canary runbook.

notes_for_operators: Canary checklist: enable autoscaler.pulse_adapter.enabled=true on canary pool, set autoscaler.quiesce.window_ms=60000, max_quiesce_ms=300000, monitor metrics.autoscaler.quiesce_delay_seconds and telemetry headroom.source=pulse. Roll back immediately if p95 latency increases by >10% for 10m.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: non-invasive estimator providing additive headroom and a conservative quiesce delay. Feature is off by default and gated for canary. Potential cost increase if max_quiesce_ms set too high; documented in runbook.
